notes:
Summary: mid-market SaaS product team evaluating Hosted API then Dedicated. Product: in-product assistant + KB search + targeted summarization for enterprise customers. Ran 14-day Hosted API trial; technical team impressed with low tail latency but wants dedicated predictability and VPC.

Trial highlights (from SE/AE notes):
- Trial period: 2026-02-16 -> 2026-03-01 (14 days).
- Calls: ~120k API calls during trial; total tokens ~18M.
- Observed avg latency: p50 ~210ms, p95 ~980ms for chat completions on hosted.
- Peak observed QPS (trial): 120 QPS burst; sustained peak window ~45 QPS for 30 minutes during product demo.
- Concurrency observed: ~25 concurrent live requests at peak demo.
- Token mix: chat/completions = 48% of calls but ~78% of token volume; embeddings = 32% of calls (~8% of tokens); reranking/small queries = 10% of calls; summarization/batch jobs = 10% but higher avg output tokens.
- Avg tokens per call (weighted): ~150 input / ~420 output => ~570 tokens per heavy chat; embeddings calls avg 75 tokens.

Business/requirements:
- Latency SLO target: p50 <= 300ms, p95 <= 1.2s. Critical for chat UX.
- Throughput needs: baseline production target = 30-60 QPS (first 3 months), forecasted scale = 180 QPS sustained (12mo growth), peak bursts expected up to 420 QPS (Black Friday-like spikes for partner events).
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget, wants committed reserved capacity for predictable unit economics; looking for a blended per-token + reserved throughput pricing.
- Security: must support SSO/SAML for admin console, audit logs retained 1 year, KMS integration for keys, and option for EU data residency for enterprise customers.
- Deployment preference: start with Redwood Hosted API in prod for 2-3 months, then transition to Dedicated capacity with VPC peering and private control plane.

Technical sizing notes (SE workshop prep):
- Initial Dedicated proposal (rough): 2 x NVIDIA A100-80GB GPU nodes as base reserved pool with autoscale to 6 GPUs for bursts. Rationale: current token profile heavy on chat + long contexts; embeddings handled by CPU/GPU mix but lower memory footprint.
- Expected concurrency per A100 (baseline): ~16 concurrency slots per GPU for chat model variant chosen. -> base concurrency ~32 slots; autoscale to ~96 slots at full burst.
- Expected sustained QPS per GPU (chat-dominant): ~20-30 QPS depending on model and batching; with 2 GPUs expect ~40-60 QPS sustained (maps to their baseline). Autoscale to 6 GPUs -> 120-180 QPS sustained, peak handling via autoscale + fallback to lower-cost model variants for extra headroom.
- Token throughput estimate: current trial extrapolated -> monthly tokens ~200M tokens at baseline (projected year-1 average). Peak months may go to 600M+.
- Pricing ask from customer: committed monthly token tiers + throughput SLA; wants a 30-40% discount vs hosted list if they commit to 12-month reserved capacity.

Conversation history (short bullets):

- 2026-03-08: security questionnaire submitted; security asks for SOC2 Type II, KMS flow diagram, VPC peering checklist. Ticket INF-4521 created.
- 2026-03-09: internal readiness call with Redwood Solutions Engineering — agreed to run dedicated sizing workshop 3/18 and produce 2 pricing scenarios (conservative / aggressive).

POC plan (customer-preferred):
- 6-week Dedicated POC after contract signature. Weeks:
  * Week 0: VPC peering + IAM + test keys.
  * Week 1-2: deploy baseline 2xA100 pool, migrate 50% traffic from Hosted -> Dedicated for smoke.
  * Week 3-4: run load test and observability checks, validate latency SLOs, exercise autoscale to 4-6 GPUs.
  * Week 5-6: compare cost per token and quality/regression checks; final sign-off meeting.

Open items for Redwood to deliver:
- Detailed capacity model (GPU type, concurrency slots, batching config) by 2026-03-25.
- Formal pricing deck + reserved capacity contract draft.
- Security artifacts: SOC2 report, KMS integration notes, VPC peering runbook.
